migration_plan: Phase 1 - Hosted proof: run openai-compat endpoints in parallel for 4 weeks, collect metrics & regression set
Phase 2 - Prompt parity pass: engineering + DX to apply prompt anchors, post-processing, and tokenization adjustments; use Redwood Optimize recommendations
Phase 3 - Dedicated eval: trial 2-week Dedicated sandbox with VPC peering and reserved pool sizing; measure sustained throughput and cost
Phase 4 - Cutover: blue-green switch using compatibility layer, gradual traffic ramp, canary rollback hooks
Phase 5 - Post-migration: quality monitoring, rollback policies, and ongoing Optimize tuning
poc_results_summary: Quality: semantic similarity on 50 eval prompts - Redwood hosted median 0.93 vs OpenAI 0.95; regressions concentrated in 7 prompts (entity recall)
Latency: p95 assistant path 210ms (hosted) vs 260ms (current provider) under 80% load
Cost: projected token spend reduction 18% on Hosted; Optimize tuning + Dedicated reserved capacity projected additional 25% savings
Operational: compatibility layer reduced migration code by ~40% vs building native adapters; still need prompt-engineering for parity
